endorsements.quote: This will ensure that AI-generated outputs support, rather than replace, human judgment and ethical responsibility.
Importantly, governance structures that embed interest holder participation and ethical review throughout the AI lifecycle are critical to maintaining public trust and social license.

Through co-design, rigorous validation, and inclusive interest holder engagement, along with careful attention to the limitations and mitigation strategies, AI can be applied in ways that support responsible and equitable implementation, strengthening rather than compromising the goals of implementation science.

Comparative evaluations against standard implementation approaches are therefore essential, including assessments of acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and downstream service and patient outcomes.

These findings highlight the importance of aligning AI-enabled implementation tools with existing workflows, resourcing models, and continuous improvement processes to support long-term sustainability and scalability.

unlisted_practices: Evaluate AI tools not only for technical performance but also for their impact on implementation processes and outcomes.
Use privacy-preserving technologies such as federated learning and secure multiparty computation to train AI without exchanging sensitive patient data.

Invest in implementation capacity, including technical infrastructure, interdisciplinary collaboration, and workforce capacity, so AI tools do not exacerbate disparities between well-resourced and under-resourced health systems.
Use explainable and transparent AI with human-in-the-loop approaches so users can understand and interrogate AI outputs.
Have implementation science experts regularly review AI-generated outputs and extracted concepts through a human-in-the-loop validation process.
Require human validation of LLM outputs used for study screening, data extraction, and evidence synthesis to mitigate errors and ensure transparency.
Policy makers should provide clear regulatory guidance, privacy-preserving data infrastructures, and accountability mechanisms for AI.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual framework and perspective article discussing how data science and AI can advance implementation science and practice, illustrated via a use-case platform (ImpleMATE).
